name: Being on the journey

claim: The cold truly is our warm friend
Cold showers make really powerful shifts that lead to a lot of awesome things
You can adapt to cold showers more than you think, with less discomfort than you think
Cold showers help in three ways
The first way cold showers help is physical: cold exposure is "absolutely proven now" to up your metabolism
The body basically produces heat through thermogenesis, shivering and non-shivering
Cold kicks both shivering and non-shivering thermogenesis into gear, shivering only initially: once you adapt a little, shivering goes away and non-shivering thermogenesis takes over
Non-shivering thermogenesis is basically the process of brown adipose tissue, brown fat, a special tissue really, really good at turning food into energy, specifically heat
The result of cold kicking thermogenesis into gear is a big metabolic boost that lasts a significant period of time, so you burn more fat throughout the day
If you're looking to drop weight or get leaner, cold showers will lead to an increase in metabolism for sure
Cold showers would probably be worth it just for the increase in metabolism

One study of cold exposure used longer exposure at not as cold temperatures, an hour (you don't need to do an hour): 68 degree Fahrenheit water, just barely cool really, gave a 93% increase in metabolic rate; 57 degree water, a 350% increase

Cold also brings a big release of norepinephrine, both a hormone and a neurotransmitter that regulates, among other things, mood, attention, focus and arousal: basically one of your feel-good hormones
The mood-boosting, antidepressive effect of the norepinephrine that cold releases is unreal
On mornings of dragging and feeling down, nothing else ever found, other than a cold shower, changed that: back in the day every energy drink known to man, coffee, all kinds of supplements
Nothing will change your state more than a cold shower
Cold is really proven to reduce your stress
With cold you feel better and more exhilarated, and more and more science now testing this on people finds a level of alertness that lasts throughout your day
There's more to the physical benefits of cold, but metabolism and norepinephrine are the two big ones
The second way cold showers help is with resistance
Resistance is what holds us back from doing what we want, pops up fears, doubts and insecurities, brings up past pain and leaves us feeling stuck
We battle resistance on an ongoing basis, and some things shift the battle in our favor
Semen retention, covered in a recent episode, is absolutely a powerful and fundamental one of the things that shift the battle against resistance in our favor

On a day-to-day basis, "I truly believe there is nothing more that you can do, nothing more powerful that you can do to start your day" and your battle against resistance from a fundamentally more powerful standpoint than a cold shower
No matter how adapted we are, a cold shower is never about comfort

A cold shower is a choice, made knowing the benefits and how much better you'll feel after, despite the discomfort: like kicking resistance in the balls right at the start of your day, saying "I am here to fight"

Kicking resistance in the balls with a cold shower at the start of your day has a ripple effect: making calls at work, deciding what to eat, getting to your workout, wherever resistance potentially pops up, you're in a more powerful position
The third way cold showers help, related to resistance but more quiet, is the meditative place
If you don't meditate, please start: it only takes 10 minutes
Meditation truly is one of the things that will change your life, helping you tap into a quiet, calm place away from anxiety and stress, and even more, the real, truest, most powerful version of you
We have a sort of quiet, still place inside, always undisturbed, full of pure light and energy and calm peace, always there no matter the storms in our head, emotions or outer world
The quiet place inside just gets obscured when we get lost in emotions, thoughts and worries
The inward journey is to find the quiet place inside and come back to it, again and again, since we keep getting pulled out
We need tools to find the quiet place inside and come back to it, and meditation is the place to start
Cold brings one of two responses. You freak out: you want to escape as fast as you can, breathe all fast, and "I'm so cold" consumes your thoughts. Or you go deeper
Just as mental and emotional storms and external events don't touch the quiet place inside, neither does your body being hot or cold, comfortable or uncomfortable
The quiet place inside is always there, warm, peaceful: not always full of laughter, there are hard times in life, but always full of peace
When you get really intentional and decide to use the cold shower to find the quiet place inside instead of wanting to escape, it will take you there, "I promise"
Cold showers can't be recommended highly enough

Used to love a long hot shower, or at least a warm one. About five or six years ago came a first exposure to cold through hardcore training methods: a lot of guys training really hard use ice baths or ice plunges, as a lot of higher-level athletes have for quite a while. During a stretch of trail running, ice baths on the legs followed really long runs, 15, 20 mile trail runs, but never really adapted to it as a lifestyle or a more frequent thing
After the ice baths came Wim Hof, "you've probably heard of him": amazing, and no better source to learn about cold, how to get so much out of it, and the breathing techniques he teaches
Look Wim Hof up if you haven't already

About three years ago, halfway through a snowy Salt Lake City winter, all bundled up, came the decision "I'm just gonna adapt". Since then, literally not more than a t-shirt, mostly a tank top. It is incredible the way we can adapt
If you tried cold showers before, you probably think there's no way you can, or want to, do it regularly; maybe you've never tried them, or once when forced to
Whether or not you tried cold showers before, a scientific process helps you deal with the cold better and better, "absolute proof" you'll adapt more than you think
The norepinephrine cold triggers also triggers an increase in brown fat, the tissue behind non-shivering thermogenesis that keeps us warmer
Brown fat is really closely linked with better health: a study of obese men showed that they had less of it
Brown fat is like the one kind of fat we do want, a special tissue we don't have a lot of and want as much of as we can, for a number of reasons, energetically too
Every time you take a cold shower or expose yourself to cold for any decent period, you build brown fat
In one study, people exposed to cold air at 60 degrees, not that cold, six hours a day for 10 days, had on average a 37% increase in brown fat
Adapting to cold is like training a muscle: you have a cold muscle
If you get cold really easily, exercise your cold muscle and it will grow and adapt like any other muscle
Brown fat is your body's engine to make heat without shivering: the more you have, the more heat you make, so along with a number of health benefits you get continually more comfortable with the cold

Shoveling snow in a tank top, out of being weird like that, a guy of habit who trains and is in gym attire a lot. The adaptation came from intending and deciding to, not from being special: the body adapted, just like yours can. Winters in tank tops or shirtless hikes are awesome too if you can get that exposure, but you don't need them: with a cold shower, you will adapt

People ask on snowy days "Aren't you cold?", and the answer is "No, not really". First, because the quiet place inside is always warm: those who have gone on some kind of inward journey know what that means, and it means so much more than the words. Beyond that, we adapt and grow brown fat, gaining an ability to produce more heat
Like anything, start easy with cold: you wouldn't walk into the gym after two years off and try to squat 300 pounds, and having never been in the cold is no reason for a 30 minute ice bath
If you're taking warm showers now, switch to cold at the end: first say 20 or 30 seconds, then a minute, over the course of say a week or two weeks
If you're taking warm showers now, after switching to cold at the end for 20 or 30 seconds, then a minute, gradually up the cold a little more
If you're taking warm showers now and gradually switch to cold at the end, after maybe three, four weeks, you'll be ready to give straight cold showers a shot
Starting cold showers easy, you will adapt, "I promise", feel amazing benefits, and not regret it

If you're sick, recovering or feel like you're getting sick, maybe you shouldn't take a cold shower? The opposite is actually true: a cold shower is one of the most beneficial things you can do to boost your immune system
Absolute science over the last several years has shown an increase in white blood cell count with cold showers
A cold shower when sick might not feel comfortable or exciting, but being sick is still absolutely a great time for a cold shower
You've got to put things into action in your life, but find the one, two or three most impactful things for you, not some 18 module course of 150 different ways to be a powerful man
Daily action on the one, two or three most impactful things for you makes a huge difference
